newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Petron Q1 net disappoints analysts.
newsitem.headline: Petron Q1 net disappoints analysts.

text.p: Oil refiner Petron Corp's first quarter earnings were a disappointement but it could still meet expectations for the year, analysts said on Thursday.
Higher margins and an improved cash flow after February's deregulation of the oil industry and more agressive marketing will help boost the bottom-line of Petron, they said.
Analysts expect Petron to post a 9.0 percent increase in net income to 4.6 billion pesos this year.
Petron, 40 percent by Saudi Arabia's Aramco, barely increased first quarter net to 1.05 billion pesos.
It sold 13.9 million barrels in the first quarter, down from 14.9 million barrels in the same period last year.
Though sales fell, Petron said it still had the biggest market share at 42 percent among the country's three refiners.

Earnings were flattened by the lower usage of fuel oil by state-owned National Power Corp which is now relying more on coal and other less expensive fuels for its generators, analysts said. This had also affected the two other oil refiners.
"Although the first quarter performance was flat, that's not indicative of how the company will perform for whole year," said Helen Alvarez, research director of All Asia Capital and Trust Corp.
"We will have to wait for the results of their enhanced marketing programme," she said.
Petron Corp early this week said it would undertake a programme to make its service stations more service-oriented and customer-friendly.
It will set up 40 new stations and refurbish 40 existing ones this year to fight stiff competition brought about by a deregulated oil industry.
Petron estimated its 1997 sales volume will exceed the projected 6.0 percent annual growth rate of the industry.
Alexis Cabel, analyst of brokerage Angping & Associates, said the new gasoline stations are expected to make up for the shortfall from fuel sales to National Power.

He sees the buying window for shares at 9.50 to 10 pesos, which is below the current market price earnings ratio of 16 times 1997 forecast earnings. The share was quoted this morning at around 10.25 pesos.
